Directions: Based on the document below and on your knowledge of social studies, answer each question that follows.
Content: If you grew up in Ireland you were told about the Famine. It was dinned [pounded] into you. In the history books there were pictures of huddled families dying of hunger in their hovels [simple dwelling], the same families being evicted — by English landlords — and with no place to go but a ditch.

In the `text(1930s)` and `text(1940s)` old people in Limerick City still whispered of the horrors of that Famine less than `text(100 years)` before. They said it was the fault of the English. They said it was a fact that `text(tons)` of corn [grain] were shipped out of the country to feed Her Majesty’s armies beyond. There was enough food to go around to feed Ireland `text(ten)` times over.
The old people said they would never forgive that of the English and they hoped we wouldn’t either...
